html:
The Abipón were an Indigenous people of the Gran Chaco in northern Argentina, speakers of a Guaicuruan language related to that of the Qom.

After the Spanish brought horses, the Abipón became mounted hunters and raiders, much as Plains peoples did in North America (horses on the Plains). In the 1600s and 1700s they raided Spanish towns such as Santa Fe and Corrientes. In the mid 1700s Jesuits founded missions for them.

The Austrian Jesuit Martin Dobrizhoffer lived among them for years and, after the Jesuits were expelled, wrote a famous account of them, published in 1784. By the early 1800s the Abipón had ceased to exist as a separate people; survivors merged into neighbouring groups.
sum: The Abipón were an Indigenous people of the Gran Chaco in northern Argentina, speakers of a Guaicuruan language related to that of the Qom.
